categories.title: Humanoid robots
categories.blurb: Bipedal and wheeled humanoids on the exhibit floor. Athletic demos sat beside warehouse and service platforms.

booths.name: Unitree Robotics
booths.blurb: G1 class bipeds, a boxing humanoid in red gloves, wheeled leg quadrupeds, and manipulation demos on the wall screens. Also ran a West Exhibit Arena slot on Monday.

booths.name: Amazon
booths.blurb: Amazon Fulfillment Innovation with yellow warehouse hardware and Digit class biped picking in a cordoned cell. The case for humanoids where human working conditions are harsh.

booths.name: Sharpa
booths.blurb: Teleoperated bartender with VR and haptic hands, then a second station under the slogan Strong, Fast, Precise. Founded in 2024.

booths.name: Booster Robotics
booths.blurb: A squad of small grey bipeds, a football, and outdoor jogging footage labelled as real footage. Aimed at labs and developers.

booths.name: EngineAI
booths.blurb: T800 class bodies sparring live. The same company behind the URKL robot fighting league. Martial arts as a stress test for balance and recovery.

booths.name: Galbot
booths.blurb: High dynamic motion all week. Their humanoid tennis work, learning athletic skills from imperfect human motion, took an IROS category award.

booths.name: Astribot
booths.meta: North American debut of the T1
booths.blurb: Upper body humanoid on a pedestal for coexistence demos. The T1’s first US showing drew a steady crowd.

booths.name: PAL Robotics
booths.blurb: TIAGo Pro Arm for advanced manipulation research, plus the familiar PAL service robot family. Robots designed to work alongside people.

booths.name: Dexmate
booths.blurb: Plug and play teleoperation and an AI first API for university labs.

booths.name: ROKAE
booths.blurb: Industrial, collaborative and embodied AI robots under one roof. Humanoid form factors next to production arms.

booths.name: Rainbow Robotics
booths.blurb: Quadruped on the carpet, dual arm mobile manipulator, and VR teleoperation.

booths.name: Sony aibo
booths.blurb: aibo Research SDK with Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab hooks. Companion morphology opened for reinforcement learning research.

categories.title: Embodied data and simulation
categories.blurb: Companies selling the missing ingredient for physical AI. Teleoperation capture, motion capture, synthetic scenes, and sim to real stacks.

booths.name: Lightwheel
booths.blurb: Physics accurate 3D assets, teleoperation in simulation, and scalable simulation for embodied AI.

booths.name: NVIDIA
booths.blurb: Isaac Sim posters and a live arm cell. The default software layer behind many demos on the floor.

booths.name: OptiTrack
booths.blurb: Truss mounted cameras and 3D tracking screens. Ground truth for locomotion, drones, and human robot interaction.

booths.name: MANUS
booths.blurb: Twenty five degree of freedom finger capture for teleoperation and dexterity datasets. Sat next to Rokoko on the mocap aisle.

booths.name: Haply Robotics
booths.blurb: Force feedback teleoperation hardware for research. The human side of data collection.

booths.name: OpenArm and open humanoid stacks
booths.blurb: Open dual arm and open framework humanoid banners. Data and algorithms meant to travel with the hardware.

categories.title: Dexterous hands and tactile sensing
categories.blurb: The quieter argument of the show. Whole body humanoids are loud. Contact is what makes manipulation reliable.

booths.name: PaXini AI
booths.blurb: Hall effect tactile sensors, e skin, gloves, hands and humanoids in one stack. Their pitch is that embodied foundation models need contact data, not only video.

booths.name: Tashan Technology
booths.blurb: AI tactile sensing chips for three dimensional force, deformation and texture.

booths.name: Analog Devices
booths.blurb: Multi finger hands, tactile driven manipulation and slip detection for deformable objects.

booths.name: BionIT Labs
booths.blurb: Adaptive underactuated hand with ten degrees of freedom and three actuators, rated IP67, for humanoids and industrial arms.

booths.name: Xynova
booths.blurb: Full stack perception, control and precision execution for general dexterous manipulation.

categories.title: Arms, mobile platforms and other systems
categories.blurb: Force controlled cobots, logistics AMRs, actuators and aerial robots. The specialist machines that already work.

booths.name: Flexiv
booths.blurb: Adaptive force controlled arms with whole body sensing and dual arm teleoperation. Specialist morphology for contact rich work.

booths.name: Franka Robotics
booths.blurb: FR3 cells for manipulation research and embodied AI demos.

booths.name: DOBOT
booths.blurb: Education and industrial cobots. A specialist form factor that does not need a humanoid body.

booths.name: Fujitsu
booths.blurb: Physical OS messaging with a white arm cell for small object manipulation.

booths.name: Robify
booths.blurb: Mobile manipulator plus AMR base. Wheeled specialty platforms for indoor logistics.

booths.name: ROBOTIS
booths.blurb: Smart actuators laid out by size. The joints inside countless research robots.

booths.name: maxon
booths.blurb: Motors and gearheads that power AMRs, arms and humanoid joints.

booths.name: HOMPO
booths.blurb: Caged multirotor hovering over its own floor sticker. Aerial robots as a specialist niche.

booths.name: CHOPTO and mini quadrupeds
booths.blurb: Miniature silver quadrupeds on the table and an orange Go2 class dog nearby.

booths.name: Bio inspired walker
booths.blurb: Entertainment and bio inspired hexapod on a green edged arena. Morphology matched to a trick, not a kitchen.

alsoVisited.name: RAI Institute
alsoVisited.note: Also on the route. Custom research platforms including the Ultra Mobility Vehicle, Roadrunner, and Koala grippers for data collection. I do not have a clean branded frame labelled RAI in this dump. If you point me at the shot, I will slot it in.
